unmatched.text: He had, therefore, offered to receive it by the hands of both Baptist and Methodist, but neither would baptize him unless he would renounce his faith in Universal Salvation.
I got religion. The sky appeared to be bluer, the leaves looked greener, and the birds sang more sweetly than ever before.

I had been told that he was a very bold man, and at the close of his discourses he challenged objectors to make known their objections. Here, thought I, will be a good opportunity for me! and hence I let a number of my brethren know that I intended to oppose him.
when he called for objections I was confounded. I could see the heads of my brethren moving to the right and left, in the crowd, expecting to see me rise to my feet. But they didn’t see me rise!
I felt certain that if I opposed Bro. Scott I would expose myself. His discourse appeared to me, at every point, invulnerable.

when called upon to close the meeting, made an excellent prayer, desiring that all might have a spirit of obedience, etc., but taking care to introduce his favorite petition that they might have a Pentecostean season and be baptized with the Holy Ghost and with fire.
Bro. Raines, what do you think of the discourse?
I can do nothing against the gospel as preached by Bro. Scott; unless I should live to disgrace it; which may our gracious Lord forbid!
I understood the first I ever heard a great deal better than I desired.
Germs of truth, and beauties and glories sprang from the bosom of that chapter under the handling of Bro Scott, of which before I had scarcely any conception.
Brother Rains, is not this so?
I have never in all my life heard just such a speaker, or just such preaching. I am sure the preacher is not inspired, but there is inspiration in what he says
He interprets the Word of God after a new fashion
I must think on these things.
Here are my notes, all of them.
Come, Brother Rains, and preach with me the everlasting gospel to the inhabitants of earth.

although I had been a preacher five years, I certainly did not know the difference between the old covenant and the new. I obtained from them a sort of hotch-potch; or rather I made of them a chaos, and preached the darkness that was on the face of the deep!
Here I virtually surrendered — not that I was convinced that all men would not be finally saved.
Bro. Scott said nothing on this subject, only that it was a philosophy, as was Calvinism, Arminianism, etc., and no part of Christianity.
He convinced me that I ought to lay my philosophy aside, and preach the gospel as the apostles preached, making their discourses a model to be accurately copied by me in all my ministrations.
I resolved that I would preach as Bro. Scott had done, and as I believed the apostles did, and that at the close of each discourse I would call for objections.

My friends, I find myself in a strait; I am shut up in a dilemma; and I can see no way out, with the Word of God in my hand, but through the obedience of faith in baptism. If any of you can see any other, I implore you in the name of my Master to show it to me.
taking hold of each other’s hands, we walked into the water. I baptized him; he in turn baptized me. I think they were all Universalists who witnessed the scene. Some cried, some scolded.
He interested himself in my favor, and had me travel and preach with him several months
By day and by night, publicly and from house to house, he was my teacher.
Often have I seen him, when he had no reason to believe that any eye saw him
prostrate on his face, pouring out his soul in prayer to God.
It was feared that they were, after all, merely baptized Universalists. If this was all, it was nothing.
I understand that you sometimes tell people that you still believe that all men will finally become holy and happy.
What then will you do with this passage: These shall go away into everlasting punishment
I will not do any thing with it. If I argue with you in defense of my opinions I shall make myself a factionist
and if you get up an argument with me, be careful, you will make yourself a factionist.
Well, sir, I’ll see whether this association will fellowship men of your views.
I will show you that I will have Thomas Campbell, A. Campbell, Walter Scott, Bentley, and a number of others on my side.
I went to that association expecting trouble
But I resolved to breast the storm.
The devil has brought this question into this association to sow discord among brethren.
Bro. Raines and I have been much together for the last several months, and we have mutually unbosomed ourselves to each other. I am a Calvinist, and he a
; and, although I am a Calvinist, I would put my right arm into the fire and have it burnt off before I would raise my hand against him.
And if I were Paul, I would have Bro. Raines
that Bro. Raines has been very badly treated, and I fear that when he speaks he will speak with too much severity.
Him that is weak in the faith receive ye, but without regard to differences of opinion.
Bro. Campbell requested me to stand upon a bench, and proclaim to the large concourse present, my own views of my obligations as a Christian and as a preacher of the gospel.
Whether there was any law of Christ by which I could be condemned?
The vote was in the negative, and in my favor by an overwhelming majority.
Brethren, I understand there are certain persons in the fellowship of this association who deny that sinners are saved by grace
I move that such persons be disfellowshiped.
I second that motion; for by grace are ye saved through faith
Now, if any member of this association holds any doctrine contradictory to the teaching of this passage, I move that he be immediately disfellowshiped.
The old Brother who had put the motion, struck a direct line for the door, and the congregation followed him; and there my association troubles ended.
so much dissatisfied were some who had come to the meeting with a view of uniting with the reformers that they declined doing so.
It gave an example, however, of a freedom of thought of which the religious community had never dreamed
His main object was to convince the people that God meant what he said in his Word, which caused great excitement
many sitting up all night reading the Scriptures to see if they meant what they said
They got their Bibles, and went to reading and searching for the truth. No word fell on the floor, or hit the wall—all was eagerly caught and tried by the book.

I also discovered that I had never read the Scriptures, to form sentiments for myself. My religion consisted in opinions, rather than faith. I had been acting upon the credit system, and I was determined to abandon it at once.
It was easily perceived the book was to be read like other books
From that time the Bible was studied as a new book, and oh, what a change it made! It is better remembered and felt than told.
The historian has to plunge into the real world
in order to find out what it is in fact that God has sovereignly done
The Meanings of History,
Suppose there exists a Shakespeare play whose fifth act had been lost.
How Can the Bible Be Authoritative?
The Old Testament has the authority that an earlier act of the play would have, no more, no less.
How Can the Bible Be Authoritative?
some of Christianity’s Great Traditions have slipped their moorings and floated off into the blue sky of speculation
The Meanings of History,
Theories of atonement do not need to be superimposed on an abstract narrative about Jesus, as has so often been attempted. They grow out of the real-life Jesus stories we already have.
The point about new creation is that it is the renewal of this world, not the substitution of another one.
The Meanings of History,
The church would then live under the ‘authority’ of the extant story, being required to offer something between an improvisation and an actual performance of the final act.
How Can the Bible Be Authoritative?
Fact means something done.
That God exists, is a truth, but not a fact; that he created the heavens and the earth, is a fact and a truth.
The first act of the great drama closes with the Deluge.
The Patriarchal Age.—No. V,
Some of those dogmas may be metaphysically true, but they are distilled truths. They have come from the Calvinistic or Arminian distillery.
It was rather a youthful performance
Its views of the atonement are rather commercial than evangelical.
It shall have for its object the developement, and introduction of that political and religious order of society called THE MILLENNIUM
The fact, or the thing said to be done, produces the change in the frame of mind.
The fruitful source of all the schism.
Faith stands on testimony. No testimony, no faith.
It could never be considered a matter of belief, since there was no testimony to render it such.

If a person say such is his private opinion, let him have it as his private opinion; but lay no stress upon it; and if it be a wrong private opinion, it will die a natural death much sooner than if you attempt to kill it.

The words and sentences of the Bible are to be translated, interpreted, and understood according to the same code of laws and principles of interpretation by which other ancient writings are translated and understood
Rules of Interpretation,

In reading the historical and epistolary parts of the sacred writings, begin at the beginning and follow the writer in the train of his own thoughts and reasonings to the end of the subject on which he writes, irrespective of chapters and verses.
Tracts for the People,
The Bible is a book of facts, not of opinions, theories, abstract generalities, nor of verbal definitions
History is therefore the plan pursued in both Testaments

Had they attempted to brow-beat me I might have been ruined forever. But treating me kindly, at the same time that they convinced me that my opinion, whether true or false, dwindled into nothingness in comparison with the faith of the gospel, redeemed me.
The facts of the New Testament will conquer the world. They have conquered me, and are now conquering thousands of others.
I am strongly disposed to reciprocate the kindness of that beloved brother, by declaring, that, if I were Timothy, father Campbell should
Reason and experience unite their testimony in assuring us that, in the same proportion as individuals labor to be of one opinion, they disagree.
